newsitem.title: GERMANY: Longer opening hours stem German retail job losses.
newsitem.headline: Longer opening hours stem German retail job losses.

text.p: The loosening of German store opening hours last November has stemmed job reductions in the sector, which employs around 2.6 million workers, the Federal Statistics Office said on Friday.
The Statistics Office said that the number of those in work rose by 1.2 percent in November compared to a year earlier, while the rise in December was 0.1 percent.

Between January and October -- before a decades-old law requiring shops to close at 6.30 p.m. on most weekdays was abolished -- the number of retail employees had fallen on a year-on-year basis by an average 1.5 percent.
New shop hours allowing stores to open until 8 p.m. on weekdays and 4 p.m. on Saturdays have increased the number of part-time workers in the retail business, the office added.
In November there were 5.8 percent more part-time workers and in December 3.1 percent more than a year earlier -- accelerating the rise of the previous 10 months, which was on average 1.5 percent.

The number of full-time workers, however, fell by three percent in November and 2.6 percent in December. That was still slower than the reduction between January and October, which averaged just below four percent, the Statistics Office said.
